cards.body: Oracle has reportedly dropped its contract with Chinese cloud provider Tencent. According to the Financial Times, the two parted ways just weeks after signing an agreement that was worth an estimated $7 billion, under which Tencent would have leased some 100,000 advanced AI chips hosted at Oracle data centers in Southeast Asia. The lease would have enabled Tencent to access Oracle's GPUs in the data centers, which are not available in China due to the US' export controls on the hardware, and was hoped to help Tencent advance its AI models and agentic tools. According to the FT and citing anonymous sources, following the agreement, US officials approached Oracle to raise concerns. Tencent also received visits from officials in Guangdong, during which it was asked to support domestic Chinese chips. Oracle, Tencent and the White House have been approached for comment. The news comes shortly after the FT separately reported that Nvidia had ordered its data center partners to reduce their exposure to Chinese customers. Sources told the FT that Nvidia has told partners that at least 51 percent of their services must go to customers outside of China. The instructions have reportedly been communicated "verbally" and not written into documentation. Nvidia said: “Data centers and clouds built on American chips are the foundation that American model and application makers need to compete worldwide. Longstanding US policy encourages every cloud to build on American infrastructure and to win business everywhere they can. America’s longstanding policy has always supported the build-out of American infrastructure worldwide, bringing prosperity, influence, and jobs home.” While Oracle has reportedly terminated the deal with Tencent, the company maintains major contracts with Chinese company ByteDance, the owner of TikTok. Previously, it was hosting ByteDance in the US, though this has since shifted with Oracle forming part of a consortium that purchased the US operations of the app to continue its operation in the country. Oracle has a large existing customer base of non-Chinese companies as well, and is a major partner of OpenAI. Tencent has been of late seeking to expand its capacity, having previously focused on internal use of compute to develop its AI offerings. In May 2026, Tencent CSO James Mitchell said: "Looking through the rest of this year, as the supply of China-designed GPUs progressively ramps up, we'll be remedying that situation; we will be making more capacity available in Tencent Cloud, and consequently driving up Tencent Cloud's rate of expansion. That's where the trade-off has been made: we have been consciously late to monetize the AI opportunity through Tencent Cloud because we've been simultaneously supporting a number of AI initiatives internally." related.title: Nvidia tells data center partners to cut China exposure, limits RTX chip sales to mainland

cards.body: Nvidia has told its data center partners to reduce their exposure to customers in China. The GPU giant has told cloud computing clients to sell at least 51 percent of their services to non-Chinese companies, the Financial Times reports. Nvidia told customers its new restrictions verbally, and not in written documents. The new rule only covers future contracts and not existing leases. With restrictions on access to Nvidia hardware in China, many Chinese companies have leased compute in Malaysia and Indonesia. Such deals could face limits under Nvidia's rules. Local cloud providers are struggling with the new requirements because it is “difficult to find enough non-Chinese clients outside the US”, one Singapore-based group told the FT. “If strictly implemented, it will definitely hurt business.” This week, Oracle reportedly dropped a $7bn deal with Tencent, which would have seen the Chinese cloud provider access as many as 100,000 Nvidia GPUs. The deal fell apart amid pressure on Oracle from US officials, as well as pressure on Tencent from Chinese officials to support domestic chips. Nvidia has already more than halved the number of Asian customers authorized to buy its AI chips. This year, it created a “white list” of companies that have passed tougher compliance checks, aimed at limiting the export of GPUs to China. While B300s are banned from export to China, the less powerful RTX Pro 5500 workstation graphics card is cleared for shipping to the country. However, Bloomberg reports that Chinese AI developers expect to receive only one percent of the chips they have ordered in the coming months. Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance and other Chinese AI and cloud firms have in total ordered about six million RTX Pro 5500 chips, but will only receive a few tens of thousands over the next four months. The low shipment number is due to capacity constraints, with Nvidia currently ramping up production. Should export controls not change, Chinese hyperscalers estimate they could receive around 700,000 RTX Pro 5500 units by the end of 2027. “Unfortunately, US firms continue to be restricted by a combination of outdated US export controls, which cover gaming products released nearly half a decade ago, and China’s own limits on US imports,” an Nvidia spokesperson told Bloomberg. The news comes following the revelation that US agencies are investigating whether Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was the victim of a Chinese spy plot, with Alice Huang (no relation to Jensen) accused of working for the Chinese state. The Megaspeed exec has been accused of sending information to China, while the Singapore-based company has been accused of sending GPUs to China. It has denied the allegations.

related.title: Nvidia can only fulfill 1% of China’s massive $70 billion GPU order for AI chips, report claims — supply constraints choke export-friendly RTX Pro 5500 deliveries despite huge demand

cards.body: Chinese technology giants ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent, among others, are set to receive only a limited number of Nvidia chips that they've ordered. Bloomberg is reporting that, according to unnamed sources, only "some tens of thousands, or roughly 1%" of RTX Pro 5500 workstation GPUs will be delivered over the next few months. Go deeper with TH Premium: GPUs (Image credit: Noctua) Desktop GPU Roadmap Nvidia's Enterprise GPU Roadmap Testing DirectStorage with GPU decompression The GeForce RTX 30-series upgrade matrix — does your Ampere GPU need an upgrade in 2026? Rubin in-depth The Stout Owl: The ultimate Noctua G2 PC Demand for the RTX Pro 5500 has far outstripped Nvidia's planned production. According to earlier reports, Chinese firms were suggested to have spent $35 billion on orders for over 3 million of the GPUs , far beyond Nvidia's ability to produce them. This new report suggests that amount has risen to $70 billion, at a cost of $11,000 per unit. Chinese demand for the RTX Pro 5500 is based on its performance and its unique status for shipping. The RTX Pro 5500 has the same CUDA cores as its flagship gaming GPU, the RTX 5090 , but with a boosted 84GB GDDR7 memory count, so it's a good option for AI. Unlike the RTX 5090, or other AI-focused workstation GPUs like the H200 and B300, there are no export limits, meaning it can be shipped to China without restrictions. China is in an arms race with the U.S. to produce better AI models, with GPUs like the RTX Pro 5500 being core to its success. Nvidia has reportedly halted RTX 5090 production to pivot towards its AI-focused enterprise base. The report suggests that Chinese developers expect a first batch of several thousand RTX Pro 5500 GPUs to be delivered by the end of 2026. In total, 700,000 RTX Pro 5500s are expected to be delivered by the end of 2027 as Nvidia increases its production, although this could change. Tom's Hardware has approached Nvidia for comment. In a statement to Bloomberg , an Nvidia spokesman declined to comment on shipment numbers, but did criticize U.S. export controls, stating that "outdated U.S. export controls, which cover gaming products released nearly half a decade ago" continue to restrict it, along with "China's own limits on U.S. imports."

key_facts: NVIDIA CUDA 13.5가 출시됨
**CUDA 13.5는 주요 신규 플랫폼에 대해 일반 가용성(GA)을 제공**

summary_data.why_matters: CUDA는 NVIDIA 가속 컴퓨팅 생태계의 핵심 소프트웨어 레이어로, 신규 하드웨어 플랫폼의 GA 지원 전환은 **해당 플랫폼이 실제 상용 배포 단계에 진입했음을 의미**한다. Vera Rubin이 개발자 프리뷰 단계를 지나 프로덕션 준비 단계로 넘어감에 따라 고객사의 대규모 도입 결정에 직접적인 신호가 된다.
summary_data.subject_angle: 소프트웨어(CUDA)와 차세대 하드웨어 플랫폼(Vera Rubin)의 동시 성숙을 통해 **NVIDIA는 하드웨어-소프트웨어 통합 전략을 지속**하며 엔터프라이즈 고객의 생산 전환을 가속화하려는 포지션을 보여준다.

key_facts: 2026년 11월 2일자 보도로 **NVIDIA가 Nscale의 Monarch Compute Campus 프로젝트를 backstop하는 논의 중**이라고 제목에 명시됨

summary_data.why_matters: AI 모델 기업 Anthropic의 컴퓨트 확보를 위해 **NVIDIA가 인프라 프로젝트에 직접 금융적 지원 역할**을 하는 것으로 보도된 점은, 칩 공급자에서 AI 인프라 생태계 조성자로 역할이 확장되고 있음을 시사한다. 이는 데이터센터 공급망·에너지 제약이 심화되는 상황에서 하이퍼스케일 컴퓨트 확보 경쟁이 자본 조달 영역까지 확대되고 있음을 보여준다.

headlines.title: Team Group CEO warns memory crisis could reach point where 'even money can't buy goods' — will get worse next year, with 'no downward trend in price whatsoever'

stage1.korean_title: 2026년 말부터 메모리칩 공급 위기 심화 예상
stage1.korean_summary: Team Group CEO가 2026년 말부터 2027년 말까지 메모리칩 공급 부족이 악화되고 가격은 하락하지 않을 것으로 예측했다.

headlines.body: Team Group CEO Chen Ching-wen said during the company’s November 2 earnings call that the memory chip shortage is expected to become worse from the end of 2026 until the end of 2027. BigGo Finance quoted Chen as saying that there is “no downward price trend whatsoever,” and that some purchasers could face a scenario “even money can’t buy goods.” He also noted that the spread between spot and contract prices for memory chips ranges from 30% to 50%, meaning short-term supply is significantly more expensive than long-term contracts. Go deeper with TH Premium: Memory (Image credit: SK Hynix) AI data centers are swallowing the world's memory and storage supply Samsung debuts three next-generation memory technologies for AI data centers The future of DRAM: From DDR5 to future ICs High-bandwidth memory roadmap Inside the history of DRAM price-fixing lawsuits "We have contracts but can't get enough volume, so we have to go to the spot market and pay a premium to grab supply," the Team Group chief said during the briefing. Contract prices for 16GB DDR5 chips climbed from $8.70 in October 2025 to $48 by September 2026. This is an increase of more than 550% in the past 12 months, and it seems that the price hikes are not letting up. He also estimated that supply and demand will not balance until the latter half of 2028 or perhaps even later. “How can prices fall when there’s nothing left?” said the CEO. The Chairman also noted that even though CXMT and YMTC have increased their market share to almost 10%, most high-end DRAM and NAND flash chips still come from Kioxia, Micron, Samsung, and SK hynix. Even then, the prices for the chips that these Chinese companies make still track the market closely , meaning they’re not the budget savior that many were expecting. As such, he expects that pricing for budget components will not ease until 2029, while high-end chips will continue to remain in short supply. These estimates go against Acer CEO Jason Chen’s prediction that component pricing will reverse by the latter half of 2027. Chen suggests that only high-end chips, like LPDDR5X-9600 and Nvidia N1-series SoCs, will remain in shortage while mainstream parts will finally go down. PCs will still experience hikes between 5% and 20% until the end of this year, plateau during the first half of 2027, before finally going down. Chen claims that most major suppliers want to hype the shortage for as long as possible to preserve their margins. Unfortunately, there’s no way for us to know which of these predictions will come true. While consumers would gladly want to have a break from the nearly continuous price hikes that PC parts and components have been experiencing over the past months, the AI data center build-out is apparently continuing , even as many Americans voted against it .

headlines.body: SambaNova has partnered with Supermicro for the deployment of SN50 RDU chips. In a statement, SambaNova said Supermicro would initially purchase 10,000 SN50 RDUs from the AI chip company in order to build and sell AI disaggregated inference systems. Those Supermicro systems will comprise both Nvidia GPUs and SambaNova RDUs, with the server maker set to integrate, test, deliver, and support the systems for customers, including providing on-site service. Meanwhile, engineers from SambaNova will ensure AI models are tuned to run on the SN50 chips, and will support Supermicro with deployments, starting with neoclouds and sovereign cloud providers, before expanding to enterprises looking to run AI in their own data centers. SambaNova first unveiled the chips, dubbed SN50 AI, in February 2026, stating that the hardware had been designed to support agentic AI workloads. At the time, the company claimed the RDUs were 5x faster than “competitive chips,” offering a 3x lower total cost of ownership, although it did not name the comparative hardware. Built using the company’s Reconfigurable Data Unit (RDU) architecture, SN50 features a three-tier memory design that supports ten-trillion-parameter models and can power “thousands of simultaneous AI sessions with consistent high performance.” SambaNova added that the chip also offers 4x more network bandwidth than its previous generation, and up to 256 accelerators can be linked over a multi-terabyte-per-second interconnect. "Agentic AI is the next wave of inference, and it has to run everywhere," said Rodrigo Liang, co-founder and CEO of SambaNova. "Supermicro builds AI infrastructure for data centers globally. Now customers can order SN50 RDUs alongside GPUs, from a world-leading partner they trust. That's how fast, efficient inference gets to scale." Charles Liang, president and CEO of Supermicro, added: “Supermicro is committed to delivering flexible, high-performance AI infrastructure that supports the evolving requirements of our customers. Our collaboration with SambaNova expands our broad DCBBS portfolio by enabling heterogeneous architectures that integrate GPU computing with specialized inference acceleration, helping customers deploy efficient, scalable AI solutions.” Founded in 2017, SambaNova previously focused on training workloads, but pivoted in 2025 to become an AI cloud services provider. Its Suite product is touted as an on-prem or cloud-based offering that allows companies to train their own generative AI models based on popular foundation models. The company first unveiled its SambaNova Cloud in September 2024. It provides cloud-based AI inference services using the company’s SN40L AI chip, launched in September 2023 and capable of running models with up to five trillion parameters.

headlines.body: AMD Cannot Catch Nvidia, But It Sure Can Make Some Money Capitalism requires strong competition to function properly, and because of that, I have always been enthusiastic about the clash of vendors and economic and technical substitution, which is not just a good idea but a law of economics. I have watched the rise of GPU compute at Nvidia from the beginning, I have watched AMD fumble and stumble and eventually become credible in datacenter CPUs (for the second time) and in datacenter GPU accelerators (for the first time with the Instinct MI200 series). But let’s be honest. AMD is hurting Intel, which has no datacenter GPU or indeed any AI accelerator to speak of, a hell of a lot more than it is hurting Nvidia. And that, I think, is mostly because AMD cannot make more Instinct GPUs because it cannot get more HBM allocations from Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron. And to be perfectly frank, AMD is selling even fewer GPUs than it otherwise might because it is loading up the HBM memory on the Instinct MI400 series a lot more than is Nvidia with its “Blackwell” B200s and B300s and its “Rubin” R200s to get a more fair balance of compute and memory capacity. I would argue that the Instinct MI500 series should have optical interposers and put disaggregated and composable HBM memory on trays adjacent to and interconnected with GPU accelerators, allowing for memory to be recycled and conserved as the GPU engines are swapped out with increasing capabilities, and that if AMD did this, it could have an intense architectural advantage over what Nvidia brings to market with static configurations that are intentionally under-memoried to ramp up GPU accelerator volumes. I doubt such a thing will happen, but it would be wonderful to see. Given the insane cost of DRAM in general, I wish the same thing for the future “Florence” Zen7 series of Epyc datacenter CPUs – trays of disaggregated and composable CPUs and DRAM banks so the DRAM can live on without having to throw it away as CPUs change. No one is expecting such a thing as far as I know, and that is one reason why AMD is not really taking market share away from Nvidia in datacenter GPUs. And AMD is taking share from Intel in datacenter CPUs not only because it has designed a superior X86 product, but because it has taken care of its process nodes and supply chain of packaging and can actually grow its X86 shipments faster than Intel – and do so at a higher average selling price. We don’t have third quarter market share numbers as yet, but generally speaking, AMD has a little more than a third of X86 server CPU shipments and a little less than half of revenues for the first half of 2026. The gap between Nvidia and AMD is growing, not shrinking, and is expected to get even wider. To keep the comparison simple, I am going to just use top line revenue across all products, which makes AMD look stronger than it is against Nvidia because of its very good client CPU and GPU businesses. headlines.title: OpenAI to rebrand its data centers as compute campuses as part of broader policy and PR push

stage1.korean_title: OpenAI 데이터센터 재브랜딩, NVIDIA도 'AI factories' 정의 중
stage1.korean_summary: OpenAI가 데이터센터를 'Compute Campus'로 재브랜딩하고 있으며 NVIDIA도 'AI factories'로 현대 데이터센터를 정의하려 하고 있다.

headlines.body: OpenAI plans to rebrand its data centers as compute campuses, as it looks to differentiate AI facilities from the broader industry. The change is part of a wider plan to shift public and political perception of data centers, as the US midterms delivered a resounding vote against the sector. "Compute campuses better describes the scale and role of the infrastructure we're building for AI," OpenAI said in a statement. "These are long-term investments in computing, energy infrastructure, and skilled work." The company hopes to use the new name to distinguish from older facilities, which may use more water or not contribute to the grid. Nvidia has separately tried to define modern data centers as AI factories. Alongside the rebrand, the company this week launched the 'Grid Protectors Program' to reduce data center electricity demand when the US grid is under strain. The non-binding pledge will see the company work with utilities, regulators, and policymakers on the program. Axios reports that OpenAI has been working on a number of policy proposals for after the midterms, including ideas for mandatory safeguards for the most powerful AI systems. "Our policy priorities — and urgency, especially on frontier safety — are about meeting the moment in response to the rapidly advancing capabilities," OpenAI chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane told the publication. "And we expect that to continue as a new Congress ramps up."

headlines.title: 나스닥 1.4% 상승에도 반도체주 급락… AI 규제 우려

stage1.korean_title: AI 데이터센터 규제 우려로 NVIDIA 등 반도체주 3.17% 하락
stage1.korean_summary: 민주당의 중간선거 승리로 AI 데이터센터 규제 강화 우려가 커지면서 NVIDIA가 3.17% 하락했다.

headlines.body: 빅테크와 반도체주 희비가 엇갈렸다. 나스닥지수는 1% 넘게 상승했지만 반도체주는 급락했다. 미국 중간선거에서 민주당이 상·하원을 모두 장악하면서 인공지능(AI) 데이터센터 건설 규제가 강화될 수 있다는 우려가 반도체주를 끌어내렸다는 분석이다. 4일(현지시각) 뉴욕증시에서 나스닥은 전 거래일 대비 1.44% 오른 2만5736.51에 거래를 마쳤다. 기술주 중심의 나스닥100지수도 0.91% 상승한 2만8437.17을 기록했다. 반도체주는 정반대였다. 필라델피아 반도체지수는 전 거래일 대비 3.13% 하락한 1만268.65에 마감했다. 장중엔 6개월 만에 가장 낮은 수준까지 떨어졌다. 반도체 종목 대부분 하락했다. 엔비디아는 전 거래일 대비 3.17% 내린 200.13달러에 거래를 마쳤다. 마이크론테크놀로지는 7.00% 급락했고, 브로드컴(-2.00%)과 SK하이닉스 미국 주식예탁증서(ADR)(-5.12%), 샌디스크(-7.91%)도 약세를 보였다. 반면 AMD는 데이터센터 매출 증가와 내년 성장 전망에 힘입어 1.01% 상승했다. 반도체주가 하락한 것은 민주당이 중간선거에서 승리한 영향으로 풀이된다. 민주당이 상원과 하원에서 모두 다수당을 확보하면서 AI 데이터센터 건설에 대한 규제가 강화될 수 있다는 가능성이 커졌다는 분석이다. 특히 데이터센터가 밀집한 텍사스와 조지아에서도 민주당이 주요 선거에서 승리하면서 관련 업계의 긴장감이 커졌다. 데이터센터 건설이 늦어지면 AI 반도체와 관련 장비 수요도 줄어들 수 있다. 골드만삭스는 민주당의 선거 승리로 일부 지역에서 데이터센터 건설을 일시 중단하는 조치가 나올 수 있고, 미국에서 계획된 데이터센터 증설 물량의 약 45%가 영향을 받을 가능성이 있다고 봤다. 스콧 크로너트 씨티리서치 미국주식 전략책임자는 로이터에 “데이터센터 건설 속도가 늦춰지거나 달라지면 관련 공급업체의 성장 전망도 바뀔 수 있다”고 말했다. 데이터센터 운영업체들의 주가도 크게 떨어졌다. 헛8은 23.23% 급락했고, 아이렌(-11.24%), 코어사이언티픽(-10.39%), 어플라이드디지털(-6.74%) 등도 동반 하락했다. 데이터센터 확장 속도가 늦어질 경우 관련 기업들의 매출 성장과 자금 조달에도 차질이 생길 수 있다는 우려가 반영됐다. 반면 자금력이 풍부한 대형 기술기업은 일제히 상승했다. 마이크로소프트가 6.68% 오른 것을 비롯해 아마존(6.12%), 애플(5.31%), 알파벳(3.18%), 메타(1.44%) 등이 강세를 보였다. 데이터센터 건설 규제가 신규 투자 부담을 줄이는 동시에 기존 인프라를 확보한 대형 기업에는 유리하게 작용할 수 있다는 기대가 영향을 미쳤다. 중간선거 결과로 정치적 불확실성이 줄어든 점도 증시 상승에 힘을 보탰다. 민주당이 의회를 장악하면서 도널드 트럼프 대통령의 주요 정책 추진에 제동이 걸릴 가능성이 커졌고, 시장에선 이 견제 구도가 증시에 긍정적으로 작용할 수 있다고 평가했다. 국제유가 급락도 투자심리 개선에 힘을 보탰다. 이날 브렌트유 선물 가격은 전 거래일 대비 8.7% 하락한 배럴당 94.62달러에 마감했다. 미국 서부텍사스산원유(WTI)도 8.3% 내린 배럴당 88.12달러를 기록했다. 민주당의 중간선거 승리로 미국과 이란 간 전쟁이 조기에 끝날 수 있다는 기대가 커지면서 유가가 급락했다. 한편 다우존스30산업평균지수는 전 거래일 대비 3.03% 오른 5만3356.12에 마감했다. 스탠더드앤드푸어스(S&P)500지수는 1.58% 상승한 7688.62를 기록했다. 윤승준 기자 sjyoon@chosunbiz.com

README:  # Nemotron 3.5 Parse ## New: DFlash2 speculative decoding **November 4, 2026:** This repository now includes an optional DFlash2 drafter in [`dflash2/`](dflash2/README.md) for faster vLLM inference. Download the model and drafter together, then point vLLM at the local draft folder: ```bash hf download nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Parse --local-dir ./parse35 vllm serve ./parse35 \ --trust-remote-code \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"./parse35/dflash2","num_speculative_tokens":32}' ``` Use a vLLM build with native Nemotron Parse and `DFlash2DraftModel` support; tested with `0.32.1rc1.dev505+g00b6c4c56` on H200/BF16. No additional model package or worker plugin is required for this path. The tested build selects Model Runner V2 automatically; older vLLM builds have not been qualified. See [draft-length tuning and throughput](dflash2/README.md#performance) below. The curve uses the best tested native draft length at each concurrency; the command above uses a fixed 32-token draft. Measurements use one H200, 2,078 ParseBench pages and three trials per point. See the [benchmark protocol and results](dflash2/performance/README.md) for settings and limitations. ### Description: Nemotron 3.5 Parse is a document image parser that produces structured, machine-readable text with semantic layout classes, bounding boxes, and reading order.
